Article Title: 'What is going on inside EC?' Union ministers, BJP allies call on poll body to clarify SIR row
Article Text:
Kumaraswamy said there was a need to distinguish between reports appearing in the media and the actual situation inside the EC

What NDA allies said

Opposition raises allegations

NEW DELHI: Union minister HD Kumaraswamy on Saturday called on the Election Commission EC to clarify amid the continuing row over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Kumaraswamy said the responsibility for addressing reports of internal differences lay with the Election Commission itself and that the country needed to know what was actually happening within the constitutional body.“It is not the question of demands by any party or any leader. The responsibility of the Election Commission, that is important. What is the ground reality? What is going on inside the Election Commission?” Kumaraswamy said.His remarks came a day after three NDA allies Chirag Paswan's LJP(RV), Upendra Kushwaha's RLM and Chandrababu Naidu's TDP separately urged the Election Commission to address concerns surrounding the SIR exercise and reports of differences within the poll panel.Kumaraswamy said there was a need to distinguish between reports appearing in the media and the actual situation inside the ECI.“The difference between what we are watching in the media and what is the real fact has to come out by these members. Because this is an important organisation, an autonomous body; why has it happened? That reality they must tell the media and the country. Their responsibility is greater. It is not an easy thing.Those three Election Commission members, including the chairman, what is the problem between them? What is the fault in that? Anything is there, they have to spell it,” he said.The issue gained traction after The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded 14 written dissents or objections over a 10-month period. The reports have prompted opposition demands for action against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and calls to halt the SIR process.The ECI has maintained that differing views, internal notes and queries are part of its institutional functioning and said its final decisions on the SIR were unanimous.LJP(RV) chief and Union minister Chirag Paswan on Friday said he did not intend to “defend what is a constitutional body” but argued that the Election Commission should address public concerns directly.“If questions are being raised about its conduct, it is the responsibility of EC, especially the chief election commissioner (Gyanesh Kumar), to present its side firmly,” Paswan said.He added: “If people start losing trust in the electoral system, that will not augur well for democracy and, therefore, I think the EC must come out with its clarification more forcefully. It need not respond to what Rahul Gandhi and his associates are saying. But it must dispel misgivings in the minds of the people.”RLM president Upendra Kushwaha also called for an immediate clarification, writing on social media, “There is considerable confusion among the public regarding the controversy surrounding SIR. This issue needs to be addressed. The EC should immediately clarify the situation to dispel this confusion.”The TDP too sought greater transparency. TDP parliamentary party neta Lavu Sri Krishna Devarayalu said, “The EC is a constitutional institution entrusted with a crucial responsibility in our democracy. Therefore, whenever questions are raised by anyone, providing appropriate clarification and maintaining transparency will only help strengthen public confidence in the institution.”Meanwhile, Jharkhand Minister Irfan Ansari criticised Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the SIR exercise and alleged that names had been removed from electoral rolls.Speaking to ANI, Ansari alleged that the ECI had acted in a manner that benefited the BJP and questioned whether the poll panel would work according to the directions of a political party. The allegations were not independently established in his remarks.“I want to ask the citizens of the country, and I even want to ask the BJP voters: Names have been removed from the voter list; your name might have been removed too,” Ansari said.He also alleged that names of Muslims, Dalits and Adivasis had been deleted from voter lists and demanded that elections in Bihar be held again.“The Commission is an independent, neutral body. No political party should interfere with it,” he said, while alleging that Kumar had interfered and helped the BJP.
Article Summary: Kumaraswamy said there was a need to distinguish between reports appearing in the media and the actual situation inside the ECI. The issue gained traction after The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had recorded 14 written dissents or objections over a 10-month period.

Article Title: NDA ally Jitan Ram Manjhi seeks more speaking time for SC/ST MPs in Parliament
Article Text:
Union minister Jitan Ram Manjhi asked the Speaker to issue necessary directions to the concerned authorities.

NDA differences over SC/ST reservation

NEW DELHI: Union minister and NDA ally Jitan Ram Manjhi has written to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, backing a BJP MP’s request for adequate speaking time for MPs from the Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) communities during parliamentary discussions on important bills.In his letter, Manjhi said BJP MP Gajendra Singh Patel, who represents Khargone in Madhya Pradesh, had raised the issue during an “NDA MPs Group Dialogue Meeting” held at Manjhi’s Delhi residence on August 5.Patel had specifically requested that SC/ST MPs be given sufficient opportunity to raise issues concerning their communities on the floor of the House, Manjhi said.The Union minister has asked the Speaker to take further action on Patel’s request and issue necessary directions to the concerned authorities.Speaking to PTI, Patel confirmed that he had raised the issue and said the time allocated to SC/ST MPs should be increased further, as the speaking time allotted to each political party is divided among its MPs.“It is not that we do not get time, but we should get more time. More issues concerning SC/ST communities should be raised,” he said.Patel said the request was aimed at ensuring that issues concerning SC/ST communities receive adequate space during parliamentary discussions, while acknowledging that MPs from these communities do get opportunities to speak.Earlier last month, differences within the NDA came to the fore over the contentious issue of sub-categorisation of SC/ST reservations, with Manjhi and fellow Bihar-based Union minister Chirag Paswan taking divergent positions on the question of reviewing the reservation system.The debate intensified after HAM(S) president and Bihar minister Santosh Kumar Suman reiterated his party’s demand for sub-categorisation of SC/ST reservations, arguing that the most deprived communities should receive a greater share of the benefits.The Supreme Court’s August 1, 2024 Constitution Bench judgment allowing states to create sub-categories within SC and ST reservations has added a new dimension to the debate.Chirag strongly opposed any review of reservation and said Manjhi and his son should resign if they supported such measures.“The constitutional provision of SC/ST reservation is based on social discrimination and not economic status. If they want to change the Constitution, then debate the issue in Parliament. Those who talk or think about reviewing reservation should first resign, as they actually want to completely end it and reduce its scope,” Chirag said.He maintained that reservation was in place yesterday, is in place today and would continue in the future.Reacting to Chirag’s demand, Suman said he was ready to resign. “As far as resignations go, we are ready. My younger brother’s party is the bigger one; they have more numbers than us and are politically third-generation too — so let them take the lead. Let him step forward by resigning and we are prepared to resign alongside him,” he said.Suman maintained that reviewing reservation did not mean abolishing it. He said HAM(S) was seeking sub-categorisation, or a “quota within a quota”, so that communities at the bottom of the social and economic hierarchy could benefit.He cited Musahar, Bhuiyan, Dom, Halkhor and Nat communities as groups that continue to face deprivation and discrimination.JD(U) national general secretary and MLA Shyam Rajak, meanwhile, opposed any discussion on reviewing reservation and warned that tampering with the system could create serious social tensions. He said reservation was a constitutional right, not charity.The reservation debate has particular political significance in Bihar, where Dalit communities are socially diverse. The Nitish Kumar government introduced the Mahadalit category in 2007 to identify the most deprived Dalit communities.
Article Summary: Jitan Ram Manjhi has written to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, backing a BJP MP’s request for adequate speaking time for MPs from the Scheduled Caste (SC) and Scheduled Tribe (ST) communities.

: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk said Thursday he feared he could be subjected to an “encounter” for speaking out against what he called atrocities in Ladakh, a year after police firing killed four protesters in Leh.Drawing a comparison with Tibet, Wangchuk said Ladakhis had chosen India because of its democracy. “Today, such atrocities are being committed in Ladakh that even China is not doing in Tibet. Wangchuk accused authorities of stopping people from attending the rally, a claim denied by police.Police said Ladakh Buddhist Association had sought permission for a public meeting at Leh’s NDS stadium, which has a capacity of 10,000. NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi is learnt to have told ministers that knowing facts and communicating them effectively was crucial as he asked them to study issues in detail and put across govt’s position to counter negative narratives.The suggestion came during the two-day Chintan Shivir at a time when issues around Election Commission’s SIR exercise and the IIT-Bombay controversy have become political flashpoints. AHMEDABAD: "Jaldi kar, Panvel nikalna hai," an alleged remark by a student during a comedy show at Nirma University in Ahmedabad has sparked controversy after a video purportedly showing a professor grabbing the student's collar went viral on social media.The incident allegedly took place during 'Technofora 2026', a three-day event organised by students of the university's Institute of Technology from September 18 to 20.According to the claims surrounding the video, a professor and head of the electrical and instrumentation department was addressing students when the student shouted the remark, referring to a dialogue from the Bollywood film 'Golmaal'.The professor then called the student on stage and allegedly grabbed him by the collar, as seen in the video.The professor is also heard threatening the student, saying, "I can go to any extent. NEW DELHI: Former Punjab chief minister Captain Amarinder Singh has expressed displeasure over not being consulted on matters concerning the state, saying he and other leaders with decades of experience in Punjab politics were not asked for their views.Speaking to PTI, Singh said, “I have spent 60 years in Punjab politics. I am not alone; there are other colleagues with me. We have seen the situation in Punjab over all these years, but at one point, they did not even ask us.”“We are people from here, and it is my duty to tell them what my views and feelings are,” Singh said, according to PTI.Singh, however, said his comments should not be interpreted as an indication that he was leaving the BJP or returning to the Congress.“I have not said that my relevance is no longer there in the Congress or the BJP. Parties keep changing,” he told PTI.“When I was in the Congress, I also went to the Akali Dal over Operation Blue Star and later returned to the Congress. That does not mean I will now leave and join another party,” Singh said.His remarks came amid questions over his political relevance in Punjab and his relationship with the BJP. Singh has been with the BJP since leaving the Congress and forming his own party, Punjab Lok Congress, before merging it with the BJP in 2022.Reacting to Singh's remarks, Punjab Aam Aadmi Party general secretary and media in-charge Baltej Singh Pannu accused the former chief minister of being an “opportunistic” political leader.“Captain Amarinder Singh is saying that he achieved nothing by joining the BJP. If a list of opportunistic leaders in Punjab were to be made, Captain Amarinder Singh would be at number one; I have never seen or heard of a more opportunistic political leader,” Pannu said, according to IANS.Pannu said Singh had already been rejected by the people of Punjab and questioned his record as chief minister.“The people of Punjab have already rejected him. Jaishankar’s pointed response to Pak journalist at UN

Three NDA partners - Chirag Paswan's LJP(RV), Upendra Kushwaha's RLM, and Chandrababu Naidu's TDP - Friday urged the Election Commission (EC) to explain its position on the political controversy surrounding the electoral process and implementation of the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, saying this was necessary to dispel doubts among the public.Paswan, LJP(RV) chief and Union food processing industries minister, told reporters in Patna he did not intend, as part of govt, to "defend what is a constitutional body", but wanted EC to address concerns among people. "If questions are being raised about its conduct, it is the responsibility of EC, especially the chief election commissioner (Gyanesh Kumar), to present its side firmly," Paswan said. He added that he had nothing to do with what the opposition said, as their job was to level allegations and politicise the issue, but the common people needed to be taken into confidence."If people start losing trust in the electoral system, that will not augur well for democracy and, therefore, I think the EC must come out with its clarification more forcefully. EC had said Wednesday that differing views among members were normal and that its final decisions had been unanimous.TDP parliamentary party neta Lavu Sri Krishna Devarayalu, while saying SIR had been a success in Andhra, where the party is in office, also sought clarification from the EC and greater transparency. Article Title: 'Compromised PM does it again': Congress targets Centre over bail for US national Matthew Aaron VanDyke held in terror conspiracy case
Article Text:
US national VanDyke was arrested by the NIA in a case involving an alleged terror conspiracy linked to Myanmar-based ethnic armed groups.

NEW DELHI: The release of US national Matthew Aaron VanDyke, who was arrested by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) in March in a case involving an alleged terror conspiracy linked to Myanmar-based ethnic armed groups, has triggered a political row, with the Congress questioning the circumstances of his release and alleging that US diplomatic pressure influenced the outcome."Our compromised PM has does it again. The PM has failed to protect India’s elections, institutions and our national security," Congress said in a post on X.VanDyke and six Ukrainian nationals were arrested by the NIA on March 13. According to the agency's allegations, the accused had entered India and travelled to restricted areas in the Northeast before crossing into Myanmar, where they allegedly came into contact with ethnic armed organisations and were involved in drone-warfare training. The NIA had initially registered the case under provisions of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).The agency's March court submissions alleged that the accused supported anti-India insurgent groups. The NIA later told a Delhi court that the seven foreign nationals were allegedly linked to a drone attack on a civilian aircraft in Myanmar, although the investigation remained underway.The case took a fresh turn on September 8, when the NIA filed a chargesheet against the seven under Sections 21 and 23 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025, without invoking UAPA provisions in the chargesheet.The agency said the UAPA investigation had not been closed and that a supplementary chargesheet could be filed if further offences were established.A Delhi court subsequently granted VanDyke default bail, observing that the chargesheet was "piecemeal" while the investigation into the UAPA offences remained pending. The 180-day statutory period for completing the investigation had also elapsed.On September 24, the court allowed VanDyke and the six Ukrainian nationals to travel to their respective countries for a month, subject to conditions. The court also released their passports.Congress has alleged that the development followed US pressure and questioned whether diplomatic intervention played a role. The party has also raised questions over how the foreign nationals obtained Indian visas and were able to travel to restricted areas of the Northeast before allegedly crossing into Myanmar.The government has maintained that the terror investigation against VanDyke and the other accused remains open.
Article Summary: US national Matthew Aaron VanDyke was arrested by the NIA in March in a case involving an alleged terror conspiracy linked to Myanmar-based ethnic armed groups. His release has triggered a political row, with the Congress questioning the circumstances of his release and alleging that US diplomatic pressure influenced the outcome.

Article Title: Combative BJP defends SIR, slams oppn for political storm
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Amid a row over the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, BJP on Friday stepped up its defence of the exercise by citing large-scale anomalies which are behind a big chunk of notices and targeted the Opposition for turning a legitimate process into an issue.Citing data, a combative BJP general secretary (organisation) B L Santhosh said less than nine months' difference among siblings is behind 6.4% of the notices issued in Delhi, while 2.5% pertain to the gap between the age of voter and parents being more than 50 years.He said 5% of notices were triggered as difference between the age of voter and parent is less than 15 years, while 4.2% notices stemmed from someone having six or more children.In 2.3% of cases, difference between the age of voter and grandparents is less than 40 years, Santhosh pointed out. He said, "Are you wondering why there's so much political storm over SIR? These are reasons. Which forces want these names to remain in the voters list? Which parties benefited from this voters' list all these years? Which party and family created a system which kept such names in voters' lists for decades? Why was SIR not held regularly all these decades? Nation wants answers for these.The aggressive response, though in keeping with BJP's stand that poll rolls needed to be cleansed to strike off illegal immigrants, the deceased and the doubly registered, stood out because it coincided with Opposition's attack on CEC Gyanesh Kumar for allegedly making decisions unilaterally about SIR which, according to it, is aimed at manipulating voter lists.
Article Summary: Citing data, a combative BJP general secretary (organisation) B L Santhosh said less than nine months' difference among siblings is behind 6.4% of the notices issued in Delhi. As questions are being raised against CEC Gyanesh Kumar for allegedly unilaterally taking many decisions pertaining to the SIR drive, a Supreme Court lawyer has filed a petition in court seeking his criminal prosecution, and another has approached the attorney general, seeking his permission, as required under the law, to file a contempt petition against him.The petition filed in SC said action needed to be taken against the chief election commissioner for his "unilateral, unauthorised, and illegal decisions" taken in the name of EC. It referred to Section 18 of Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, and the law laid down by a constitution bench in the TN Seshan case in 1995 to say EC's decisions mandatorily had to be taken by the majority.EC has maintained that all the decisions regarding special intensive revision of electoral rolls were taken unanimously by Kumar and his two colleagues, election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.The petition filed by advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi, echoing claims made in a news report, sought quashing of unauthorised modifications made to Form 6 on ECINet/ERONet portals requiring ancestry/last-SIR declarations, and also sought immediate restoration of the statutory Form 6 as prescribed under Registration of Electors Rules to permit all eligible adults to register as voters on the basis of original statutory requirements.Mentioning the alleged illegal acts of CEC, the petition said, "Introducing a mandatory ancestral condition (last SIR linkage) for first-time young voters without legislative authority or amendment of Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, was explicitly branded as unauthorised and illegal by a majority of the commission."The petition said depriving decentralised electoral registration officers of their statutory authority under sections 13B, 22 and 23 of Representation of the People Act, 1950, and centralising electoral roll management under the director general of IT in Delhi was another wrong."Tampering with the electoral roll constitutes a cognisable offence under Section 32 of RP Act, 1950, as well as provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita concerning falsification of records and public servants disobeying directions of law. In such a scenario, divested of any statutory or constitutional immunity, CEC remains directly accountable under the law - subject to police investigation, evidence gathering, and regular trial proceedings as an ordinary accused," the petition said, adding CEC could not claim immunity for illegal acts.It said CEC's act of deliberately manipulating the electoral roll bore no "reasonable nexus" or legal connection to his official duties and fell squarely outside the ambit of official immunity and constituted distinct, personal criminal liability.Another apex court advocate, Shiv Kumar Tripathi, wrote to the attorney general, bringing to his notice the "constitutional misconduct and contempt of court" by CEC and sought his approval to file a contempt case against him."SC has repeatedly emphasised EC's independence, impartiality and institutional integrity. CEC's office is one of constitutional primacy, but it is not intended to function as an authority overriding the equal constitutional status of other election commissioners in collective decision-making. Any departure from this constitutional framework may undermine public confidence in free and fair election," Tripathi said in his letter."I therefore respectfully request your good office to examine whether the reported conduct amounts to wilful disregard of binding judicial principles or directions of the Supreme Court, thereby attracting proceedings under Contempt of Courts Act, 1971, if legally sustainable," the letter said.

Article Title: Uttarakhand CM Dhami directs officials to maintain vigilance amid red alert in several districts

Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami , in view of the red alert issued by the India Meteorological Department (IMD) for the next two days, spoke to Secretary Disaster Management and Rehabilitation Vinod Kumar Suman and directed all concerned districts and departments to take necessary precautionary measures.Dhami directed officials to maintain heightened vigilance in districts under red and orange alerts, continuously monitor vulnerable areas and ensure that all arrangements for relief and rescue operations are in place in advance in case of any emergency. He also directed that district emergency operation centres remain active and weather warnings be disseminated immediately at the local level.Disaster management and rehabilitation minister Madan Kaushik also spoke to Secretary Vinod Kumar Suman and took stock of the weather situation and preparedness across the state. He directed officials to closely monitor the weather and remain fully prepared to deal with any eventuality.Following the chief minister’s directions, Secretary Vinod Kumar Suman held a meeting with all 13 districts on Friday and instructed them to remain on alert mode.According to the weather department forecast, on September 26, red alerts have been issued for five districts, orange alerts for five districts and yellow alerts for three districts.On September 27, red alerts have been issued for four districts, orange alerts for four districts and yellow alerts for five districts.On September 26, Bageshwar, Pithoragarh, Champawat, Nainital and Udham Singh Nagar are under a red alert, while Dehradun, Pauri Garhwal, Rudraprayag, Chamoli and Almora are under an orange alert. Haridwar, Uttarkashi and Tehri Garhwal are under a yellow alert.On September 27, red alerts have been issued for Dehradun, Tehri Garhwal, Pauri Garhwal and Haridwar; orange alerts for Uttarkashi, Chamoli, Nainital and Rudraprayag; and yellow alerts for Bageshwar, Almora, Champawat, Udham Singh Nagar and Pithoragarh.The weather department has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall at several places and extremely heavy rainfall at isolated places. Authorities have been asked to remain particularly vigilant in view of the possibility of landslides and road blockages in hilly areas, rising water levels in rivers and streams, and waterlogging in the plains.Suman directed all districts to continuously monitor vulnerable areas, keep district emergency operation centres operational and ensure immediate dissemination of every weather warning to the ground level.Officials have been instructed to continuously monitor water levels in rivers, streams, gad-gaderas and other water sources and make arrangements to shift people living nearby to safer locations if water levels rise. JCBs and other necessary machinery should be stationed at strategic locations along landslide-prone roads and areas so that blocked routes can be cleared at the earliest.All district emergency operation centres have been directed to remain operational round the clock, with continuous coordination among the police, SDRF, fire services, health, Public Works Department, drinking water, power and other concerned departments. Relief and rescue teams, along with necessary equipment and resources, should be deployed in vulnerable areas as required.The secretary also directed that traffic on mountain routes be regulated based on weather and road conditions and unnecessary travel in areas vulnerable to landslides and heavy rainfall be avoided. People living near rivers, streams and seasonal water channels should be regularly alerted and prevented from approaching riverbanks or entering fast-flowing waters.Special monitoring has also been ordered along the Char Dham routes, major tourist destinations and other vulnerable areas to ensure the safety of pilgrims and tourists. All arrangements should be kept ready in advance so that relief and rescue operations can begin with minimum response time in case of an emergency.Suman urged district administrations to remain fully alert and not to show any negligence in view of the prevailing weather conditions. He also appealed to the public to follow advisories issued by the weather department and district administration, avoid unnecessary travel and stay away from rivers, streams and landslide-prone areas.The State Emergency Operation Centre is continuously monitoring the weather situation. In case of any emergency, people can contact the State Emergency Operation Centre at toll-free number 1070, the District Emergency Operation Centre at 1077, or emergency services at 112.
Article Summary: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami spoke to Secretary Disaster Management and Rehabilitation Vinod Kumar Suman. He directed officials to maintain heightened vigilance in districts under red and orange alerts. Suman urged district administrations to remain fully alert and not to show any negligence in view of the prevailing weather conditions.

Article Title: Unease within NDA over EC-SIR row? Three BJP allies seek poll body clarification as opposition keeps up pressure
Article Text:
What is the controversy

NEW DELHI: Unease within the ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA) over a media report concerning Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar surfaced on Friday, with three BJP allies urging the Election Commission of India (ECI) to issue a clearer response.Union minister and Lok Janshakti Party (LJP) president Chirag Paswan was the first NDA ally to urge the ECI to dispel “misgivings in the minds of the people.”“Let me make it clear that, as part of the government, I do not intend to defend what is a constitutional body. I am also not much worried about the allegations made by the opposition, which will always take a stand that suits it politically,” Paswan told reporters in Patna.“However, if people start losing trust in the electoral system, that will not augur well for democracy. Therefore, I think the Election Commission must come out with its clarification more forcefully. It need not respond to what Rahul Gandhi and his associates are saying, but it must dispel misgivings in the minds of the people,” the Hajipur MP added.Rashtriya Lok Morcha (RLM) chief and Rajya Sabha MP Upendra Kushwaha also called for a clarification, saying the controversy had created “confusion” among the public."The controversy regarding the SIR has created a situation of significant confusion among the public. The matter needs to be addressed. The Election Commission should immediately issue a clarification regarding the actual situation to clear up this confusion," Kushwaha posted on X.The Telugu Desam Party (TDP) described the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise in Andhra Pradesh as a “success,” while noting that a clarification from the ECI would be “beneficial”.“The exercise has been a success. Even the opposition has not been able to substantiate its concerns regarding the process in Andhra Pradesh. At the same time, the Election Commission of India is a constitutional institution entrusted with a crucial responsibility in our democracy. Therefore, whenever questions are raised by anyone, providing appropriate clarification and maintaining transparency will only help strengthen public confidence in the institution,” TDP MP Lavu Srikrishna Devarayalu said.The allies’ remarks came after a report in The Indian Express said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had, on at least 14 occasions over the past 10 months, recorded objections to decisions and orders apparently issued without their knowledge or recommendation.The objections reportedly related to changes to the statutory voter registration Form 6, the process for adding and deleting names from electoral rolls, and the centralised control of the electoral roll database.The report prompted opposition parties to demand the CEC’s removal and call for the SIR exercise to be halted.The ECI, however, asserted that differences of opinion among its members were a “normal part of deliberation” and maintained that its final decisions, including those concerning the SIR, had been “unanimous”.According to the Commission, all its official orders and directions had legal sanction, while describing the suggestions made by the two Election Commissioners as efforts to improve electoral processes. Neither Sandhu nor Joshi has publicly commented on the objections attributed to them.The BJP, meanwhile, has played down the reported differences within the Commission, saying that the exchange of views during official deliberations reflected “pure democracy." The saffron party's West Bengal unit chief, Samik Bhattacharya, for instance, suggested that Gyanesh Kumar be awarded the Padma Bhushan, the country's third-highest civilan honour."The fact is, even the Congress party itself doesn't heed Rahul Gandhi's words; they don't take him seriously... Gyanesh Kumar deserves, at the very least, the Padma Bhushan... In a border state like this (West Bengal), Gyanesh Kumar took the initiative to remove the names of Bangladeshi infiltrators from the voter list," Bhattacharya said.Kumar, who became an Election Commissioner in 2024 and CEC in 2025, has repeatedly faced allegations from the Opposition that he has “favoured” the BJP.
Article Summary: Three BJP allies urge the Election Commission of India to issue a clearer response to a media report. Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar has faced allegations from the Opposition that he has “favoured the BJP” The report prompted opposition parties to demand the CEC’s removal and call for the SIR exercise to be halted.

NEW DELHI: West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya has come out strongly in support of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar amid a growing Congress-led campaign against him. Bhattacharya said that Kumar deserves "at the very least, the Padma Bhushan " for overseeing peaceful elections and changes to the electoral rolls in the state.Bhattacharya also took a swipe at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi , claiming that even members of his own party do not take his statements seriously."The fact is, even the Congress party itself doesn't heed Rahul Gandhi's words; they don't take him seriously... Gyanesh Kumar deserves, at the very least, the Padma Bhushan," Bhattacharya said while speaking to reporters.Praising the conduct of elections in West Bengal, the BJP leader said voters were able to cast their ballots without fear or intimidation."The people of West Bengal are delighted that, after so long, intimidation was kept at bay. There were no incidents of murder, and people were actually allowed to cast their votes. Furthermore, in a border state like this, Gyanesh Kumar took the initiative to remove the names of Bangladeshi infiltrators from the voter lists," he added.Bhattacharya said the measures taken by the Election Commission had received broad public support."The people of West Bengal have rarely witnessed an election like this. Therefore, the general public of West Bengal fully supports Gyanesh Kumar..." he said.His remarks came as Congress stepped up its protests against the Election Commission across the country, with party workers demanding Kumar's resignation over the poll body's functioning and the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.In Delhi, the Indian Youth Congress marched from Raisina Road to Jantar Mantar, raising slogans against the CEC and demanding his resignation.The protests also spread across several states. In Patna, police used water cannons to disperse Congress workers demonstrating against Kumar. In Chandigarh, similar scenes were reported as police used water cannons against protesting Congress workers, some of whom climbed onto police vans.Congress workers also held demonstrations in Jammu and Kashmir, Assam, Uttarakhand, West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh and Manipur.In Shimla, Congress leaders and workers protested outside the State Election Commission office over issues concerning the Election Commission. Protesters also blackened the official board outside the office.In Manipur, Congress workers led by PCC president Okram Ibobi Singh and Congress Legislature Party leader Keisham Meghachandra Singh marched towards the chief electoral office at Lamphelpat. Protesters demanded Kumar's arrest and prosecution and burnt an effigy of the CEC.The protest later turned tense, with demonstrators scuffling with police. Security personnel fired tear gas shells to disperse the protesters.In Jammu, heavy police deployment was reported outside the Election Commission office, while Congress MLAs in Srinagar protested inside the Legislative Assembly, carrying banners demanding Kumar's resignation.Demonstrations were also held in Lucknow, Guwahati and Kolkata.The nationwide protests are part of Congress' campaign against the functioning of the Election Commission and its handling of the SIR exercise.The political confrontation has intensified following an Indian Express report that election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months regarding decisions and procedures related to electoral rolls and access to election databases.The Election Commission has rejected the allegations, saying decisions related to the SIR were taken unanimously and that written notes, observations and differing views were part of its internal deliberations.
Article Summary: West Bengal BJP president Samik Bhattacharya has come out strongly in support of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. He said Kumar deserves "at the very least, the Padma Bhushan " for overseeing peaceful elections and changes to the electoral rolls in the state. His remarks came as Congress stepped up its protests against the Election Commission across the country.

Article Title: Bodies of 4 Tangkhul Naga men allegedly killed by militants found near Myanmar border in Manipur
Article Text:

Bodies of the four men, belonging to the Tangkhul Naga community who were allegedly killed by militants, were found in Manipur's Kamjong district.The bodies of the four men, identified as Vareishim Jajo, Phami Jajo, Betterson Jajo and Ningthem Kashak, were found at an isolated spot near the Myanmar border in remote Pilong village around 1.30 am on Friday, police said. The bodies bore multiple bullet marks and were found after a prolonged search by police and locals, reported PTI.Police said the bodies were being brought to Kamjong district hospital for post-mortem examinations. Pilong village is around 34 km from the district headquarters.Locals alleged that militants from neighbouring Myanmar crossed into India and ambushed a group of five villagers on Thursday, before the bodies were found. One of the villagers managed to escape and alerted local authorities. However, the search for bodies continued till early Friday.“Villagers claimed that four persons were killed when militants from neighbouring Myanmar crossed the border and attacked five people. One of them managed to escape and reported the incident to the villagers and the local authorities. The killing has not been confirmed. A police team has been dispatched to ascertain the claim," the officer had said.Naga Peoples' Front state president Awangbou Newmai condemned the killings and alleged that members of the Kuki National Army (Burma) were behind the attack. He appealed to all communities to "shun violence" and "co-exist as peaceful neighbours".The killings come amid a fresh escalation in Kuki-Naga violence in Manipur that has spread across parts of Ukhrul, Kamjong, Kangpokpi, Tamenglong and Noney districts since February. What began with clashes between Tangkhul Naga and Kuki communities in Ukhrul in February has developed into a wider cycle of ambushes, attacks on villages and civilian killings.In recent weeks, attacks have been reported on both communities. Four Kuki villagers were killed in separate attacks in Tamenglong and Noney on September 13, followed by attacks on Naga settlements and the killing of a Naga teenager in subsequent days.A 36-year-old Kuki electric lineman was also killed in an attack on Kuki settlements along the IT Road corridor in Kangpokpi on September 23, while Naga villages along the Noney-Kangpokpi-Senapati borders came under attack the same day.The latest violence has occurred despite a heavy security presence in the state, with the Army, Assam Rifles, CRPF, BSF, ITBP and SSB deployed in affected areas. The violence has also increasingly involved allegations of attacks by armed groups operating along the Kuki-Naga fault line, although responsibility for individual attacks is often disputed or remains under investigation.
Article Summary: Bodies of four men, belonging to Tangkhul Naga community, found in Manipur's Kamjong district. The killings come amid a fresh escalation in Kuki-Naga violence in Manipuri.

Article Title: Omar’s resolution on J&K’s statehood fuels autonomy debate in J&K House

BJP rejects Omar’s statehood resolution, opposes Article 370 debate

SRINAGAR: Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah today brought a resolution before Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly seeking the restoration of full statehood to Jammu and Kashmir. However, the resolution was fiercely opposed by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) creating chaotic scenes forcing the speaker to adjourn the House.As the resolution contains a reference to the autonomy resolution passed by J&K Assembly in June 2000, when Jammu and Kashmir was a state, the BJP accused the ruling party of being anti-national and called the resolution an autonomy resolution.Omar’s resolution reads: "In addition to the resolutions passed by this House on 26 June 2000 and 6 November 2024, the House calls upon the Government of India for the immediate and urgent restoration of full statehood to Jammu and Kashmir and resolves that this resolution be forwarded to the Government of India."For nearly two years, Chief Minister Omar Abdullah has repeatedly called for the restoration of statehood and taken up the issue with the Centre. Soon after taking office, his Cabinet passed a resolution seeking restoration of statehood.NC legislators said the Centre’s lack of movement on statehood forced the party to bring the resolution in the Assembly. Omar echoed this, saying it seems the cabinet was not seen as the sole voice of the people, while the legislature represented the broader political spectrum of Jammu and Kashmir including parties outside the government.“Statehood is not about the government or my family, it is about Jammu and Kashmir. That is why we brought it to the House, so that a united voice can go to the Centre for restoration of statehood,” Omar said.After Omar moved the resolution, the BJP legislators shouted slogans, tore copies of the resolution. Incidentally Congress legislators supported the resolution even moved towards the well to confront BJP legislators. The BJP argues that the resolution shouldn’t have mentioned autonomy resolution in the statehood resolution. Angered by the BJP legislators’ slogans, some of the NC legislators displayed papers reading “we want autonomy of J&K be restored. ” Others called for restoration of Article 370 Earlier addressing the House after moving the resolution, the CM said the House should discuss and pass the resolution as lack of statehood to J&K is causing immense suffering to people of J&K.“We were promised that the restoration of statehood would follow delimitation and elections. Delimitation of constituencies was carried out. Elections were held and a large number of people took part in them (in 2024). People voted without any coercion. But the third step of the promise, the restoration of statehood was not fulfilled,” Omar said, referring to assurances given by the centre in Parliament and before the Supreme Court.The CM said statehood was a promise made by the government of India and reaffirmed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in a function where he was present along with the leader of Opposition in J&K Sunil Sharma . He said the Prime Minister has stated that the restoration of statehood is Modi’s promise.Omar said several important institutions and projects remained beyond the effective control of the elected government, citing the Power Development Corporation and AIIMS-related matters as examples.“As chief minister and power minister, I do not receive the files of the J&K State Power Development Corporation. If the elected government is responsible for everything other than security, law and order, and services matters, then why are institutions like the State Power Development Corporation or health institutions like SKIMS outside its control,"J&K CM added.Explaining the adding previous resolution to the current resolution, he said the House continued to stand by all resolutions passed earlier by the Assembly. He said he has mentioned earlier resolutions in the current resolution so that “our friends” an indirect reference to the PDP shouldn’t say that “we have given up on them.” “Those resolutions remain in place. This House owns them. This resolution neither replaces nor ignores them. It is an addition to them,” he said.Omar said the resolution simply called upon the Government of India to fulfil its commitment and restore full statehood to Jammu and Kashmir. “We do not want a half state, a quarter state or a state without powers over law and order. We were promised full statehood and full statehood is what we seek,” he said.“We wanted a resolution to be passed by the Assembly and sent to the Government of India stating that Jammu and Kashmir’s statehood should be restored immediately,” he said.Later talking to reporters Omar said, “elections were held almost two years ago and a promise was made to restore statehood to Jammu and Kashmir.” He said the promise has not been fulfilled. “We are asking the BJP to vote only on statehood. We are not asking them to vote on Article 370, special status or autonomy. Those resolutions have already been passed by this House.”The chief minister rejected BJP’s accusation that his resolution is an anti-national stating, “how can demanding statehood be anti-national? What is anti-national about it? We have not brought a resolution on autonomy. Those resolutions have already been passed by the House. They remain the property of the House. We are not touching them. This new resolution is only about restoring statehood and does not dilute the earlier resolutions. ” However, he said, if the BJP wants to bring a resolution to replace or reject the earlier resolutions, they should do it. “We are a democracy.”
Article Summary: Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah today brought a resolution seeking the restoration of full statehood to J&K. The resolution was fiercely opposed by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) creating chaotic scenes forcing the speaker to adjourn the House. BJP accused the ruling party of being anti- national and called the resolution an autonomy resolution.

Article Title: ‘Corruption under CM’s nose in Punjab’: Congress questions why ED acted before elections
Article Text:
Warring questions ED’s election-time action

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Punjab Congress chief Amrinder Singh Raja Warring on Friday questioned the Enforcement Directorate 's timing in carrying out searches in the state, alleging that corruption had taken place in several departments under the "chief minister's nose".Warring said alleged corruption in Punjab must be investigated, but questioned why central agencies had become active only ahead of elections."I have never given a clean chit to any central agency, because central agencies tend to become active only around election time. But yes, the fact remains that within Punjab, not just GMADA [Greater Mohali Area Development Authority]—there are many other departments and ministries where scams on a massive scale have occurred," Warring told reporters."Those scams must be thoroughly investigated, and this corruption was taking place right under the chief minister’s nose," he added.Taking a swipe at those allegedly involved in the irregularities, Warring said people in Punjab were aware of what had happened."Don't just take my word for it; as an opposition party chief, I am bound to say this, but ask anyone, ask the common people: it wasn't some foreign invader like Ahmad Shah Abdali who looted Delhi; the looters were specific individuals whose names are now surfacing," he further said.Warring said the ED action was welcome but questioned why similar action had not been taken earlier."All this happened under the chief minister's watch. Yet, questions also arise regarding the ED: Why have you become active only now?" he said."It is good [that action is being taken], but during the past five years when Punjab was crying out in protest, you knew that the policies of Delhi were formulated here... that the Delhi policies were mirrored here. Why were you silent back then? What were you waiting for?" he asked."Were you waiting for Punjab to be plundered? For Punjab to be stripped clean? Were you waiting for Rs 10,000 crore to be stashed away before stepping in? Why didn't you arrive earlier? And why right before elections?" Warring said.The Congress leader also raised the possibility of a "collusion at the top", but stressed that this was his own assessment."Often I am fully convinced that there is collusion at the top. It's staged—like staging protests where you pretend you're being victimised, and they respond... but beneath the surface, behind closed doors, there's collusion," he said.He also sought answers on cases and FIRs registered earlier, questioning whether those investigations had progressed."And what happened to the major FIRs and cases filed earlier? You made huge claims back then too," Warring said."Corruption has taken place. Corruption has occurred across ministries and right under the chief minister’s nose. But my question remains for the ED: Why this delay? Why did you stand by watching Punjab get looted?" he said.Warring also referred to speculation about an alleged understanding involving the Union home minister and differences within the Aam Aadmi Party "Some people even speculate that the Home Minister... these are speculations, of course. There are internal rifts within AAP as well, infighting among them... perhaps they want to wrap up those speculations too," he said."What the hidden secret is will be revealed gradually. I won't say it outright today. When I say Home Minister, I mean the Union Home Minister of the country. So, where this loop originates, who is in league with whom, and who wants to frame whom—all of this will become clear in the days to come," he added.The ED on Tuesday carried out search and survey operations at 26 premises across Delhi, Chandigarh, Haryana and Punjab as part of a money laundering investigation linked to Tirupati Infraprojects Pvt Ltd.The agency also surveyed the GMADA office and the Punjab government's Department of Housing and Urban Development.The ED said its investigation found that the promoters of Tirupati Infraprojects also controlled other entities that bought two prime auction sites in Mohali from GMADA. These entities later received substantial financial relief on dues owed to the authority, according to the agency.The agency has estimated the suspected undue gain to the companies and the resulting loss to the exchequer at more than Rs 100 crore.The searches have since turned into a political flashpoint in Punjab. The ruling AAP has accused the Centre of using central agencies against the state government ahead of the 2027 assembly elections. AAP leaders and workers also held a protest outside the GMADA office in Mohali on Thursday.
Article Summary: Punjab Congress chief Amrinder Singh Raja Warring questions the Enforcement Directorate's timing in carrying out searches in the state. Warring alleges corruption had taken place in several departments under the "chief minister's nose" The ED on Tuesday carried out search and survey operations at 26 premises across Delhi, Chandigarh, Haryana and Punjab.

Article Title: Veeramani Pocso case: Photo of TVK minister with Gem Granites chief surfaces; DMK says 'take action'
Article Text:
Child rape: Granite baron Veeramani’s premises raided

SIT formed as probe expands

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: DMK spokesperson T K S Elangovan hit back at allegations linking the party to Gem Granites chairman R Veeramani, saying the DMK should not be blamed for the alleged actions of an individual. His remarks came as Chennai police constituted a four-member Special Investigation Team (SIT) to probe allegations of sexual offences against minor girls involving Veeramani.“They want to accuse the DMK for all those things. Today, there was a photograph on social media showing two ministers sitting with Veeramani. I don't understand anything,” Elangovan said.He added that Veeramani had been arrested and that the party leadership had also called for action if he was found to have committed any wrongdoing.“They have arrested him, and our leader also issued a statement that if he has committed a mistake, take action,” Elangovan said.Earlier, while talking to ANI, advocate and DMK leader NR Elango said "TN minister CTR Nirmal Kumar has falsely stated that the Veeramani case was diluted during the DMK regime. The case was registered on 07.12.2025 and investigated by the police. Houses were searched and further investigation was conducted based on the available evidence.The police had only stated that since adequate evidence was not yet available, complete investigation reports have not been filed so far, and that the further investigation is deferred until proper evidence is obtained—not that the case was dropped. The investigation was never dropped during the DMK regime."An SIT team has been formed as the investigation expands following the arrests of Veeramani and his associates.The SIT will be headed by Additional Commissioner of Police PC Thenmozhi of the Central Crime Branch. Joint Commissioner of Police N Disha Mittal, Superintendent of Police Mutharasi and Deputy Commissioner of Police Geethanjali of the Central Women and Children unit are the other members of the team.Veeramani was arrested along with Shanthi and Mahendra Simhan on August 29 in connection with the POCSO case. A former Gem Granites employee, Ganesan, was subsequently arrested on September 22 after police allegedly found a video linked to the case on his mobile phone.Veeramani was arrested after a USB drive containing a video clip that purportedly showed a juvenile girl being sexually assaulted by him in Oct 2025. Police said they identified the survivor and established that she was a minor when the alleged offence took place in 2019.
Article Summary: DMK spokesperson T K S Elangovan hit back at allegations linking the party to Gem Granites chairman R Veeramani. He said the DMK should not be blamed for the alleged actions of an individual. His remarks came as Chennai police constituted a four-member Special Investigation Team to probe allegations.

Article Title: 'Must maintain the trust of people': Chirag Paswan urges EC to 'firmly present its side' amid SIR row
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Union minister Chirag Paswan on Friday urged the Election Commissioner to "firmly present its side" amid the ongoing row over the internal disagreements in the poll panel.Speaking to reporters, Chirag said the Election Commission must retain people's trust and address their doubts about the electoral process."If such questions are being raised against the Election Commission, I believe it is also the responsibility of the Election Commission, especially the CEC, to firmly present its side," the Union minister said."I don't care what the opposition says because it is their job is to do politics. The Election Commission must maintain the trust of the people because if doubts arise in the public's mind about the electoral process itself, that would be wrong. In such a situation, the Election Commission should firmly put forth its points so that no doubts arise in the people's minds," he added.This comes after the opposition demanded Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation after an Indian Express report highlighted differences among members of the EC over the SIR of electoral rolls.The report said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi raised formal objections on at least 14 occasions over a 10-month period against decisions and orders related to electoral-roll processes.Earlier on Thursday, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi accused the CEC of "vote chori, kanun chori, sanstha chori (vote theft, law theft, institutional theft)", calling it an "act against the nation"."The Election Commission is the institutional protector of the vote... I have shown it with proof, and there is already more than enough information to make this a 100% certainty that Indian elections, Lok Sabha elections, 2024 election, Vidhan Sabha elections are all being rigged," he said, addressing a press conference.The Election Commission, however, described the queries and observations raised by its members as part of its routine internal process. It said written notes, technical inputs and internal scrutiny were standard mechanisms to check legal compliance and protect voters' rights.The ECI further said all decisions taken by the Commission, including those related to SIR, had full legal backing and stressed that its final decisions were unanimous.
Article Summary: Union minister Chirag Paswan on Friday urged the Election Commissioner to "firmly present its side" This comes after the opposition demanded Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. An Indian Express report highlighted differences among members of the EC over the SIR of electoral rolls.

Article Title: US ambassador to India Sergio Gor makes rare appearance at event hosted by Chinese envoy

Sergio Gor
