Article Title: Veeramani child rape case: Vijay slams previous DMK govt’s failure to take action, asks “what kind of a deal was struck, sir?’
Article Text:
Vijay campaigning for TVK candidate K Maragatham in Madurantakam assembly constituency on Friday. Photo by L R Shankar





MADURANTAKAM: Without explicitly referring to the sex scandal involving granite baron R Veeramani, Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Friday condemned the previous DMK govt for failing to take appropriate action against an “individual accused of abusing and exploiting young children for years. ”"Something truly atrocious is happening right now. I initially thought about not bringing up this issue here, but a person has been exploiting Tamil Nadu’s young girls and children for years. Although the case surfaced during the previous DMK tenure, the matter and its history were quietly buried. What kind of a deal was struck, sir? The entire state of Tamil Nadu is questioning this," Vijay said while campaigning for TVK candidate K Maragatham in Madurantakam assembly constituency where a byelection will be held on Oct 6.Vijay turned the sensitive issue into a powerful campaign tool. He said, "Stalin sir (DMK chief MK Stalin), open your mouth and speak up. Others alongside you are also keeping quiet. Is there an unspoken understanding or collusion keeping you from speaking out on this issue?"He went on to criticize the DMK and its allies for posing as defenders of women's rights. "We were the ones who imprisoned that person," he stated."If you cannot step forward and address the pain and anguish of these young children, what kind of politics have you been practicing all these years? The people must teach the DMK and its allies a fitting lesson in the upcoming bypoll," Vijay added.READ ALSO: 'Don’t touch this Vijay, you will regret it'
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay condemned the previous DMK govt for failing to take appropriate action against an “individual accused of abusing and exploiting young children for years’ Vijay was campaigning for TVK candidate K Maragatham in Madurantakam.

Article Title: 'Could endanger his life': Imran Khan's son warns against Adiala jail protest
Article Text:
Imran Khan's son warns against Adiala jail protest

Former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan 's son Kasim Khan has urged Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) supporters not to march towards Rawalpindi's Adiala jail during the party's planned September 27 protest, warning that such a move could be used by Pakistani authorities as a pretext for a "counter" assault on the prison and put his father's life at risk.The warning comes ahead of the PTI's planned protest and march, which is being held to demand Imran Khan's release.The former premier has been in prison since August 2023 following convictions in multiple cases.In a post on X, Kasim said he had been asked to appeal to supporters against gathering near Adiala jail."I’ve been instructed to call on the public not to attempt to march or protest nearby Adiala jail on 27. I’ve heard from sources that this may be used as an excuse for the establishment to launch a “counter” assault on the jail (Which my father is being held in), which could endanger his life. Please do not give them any reasons for “accidents” to happen to my father during the protest," Kasim's post read.His appeal comes as security measures have been stepped up across Punjab ahead of the PTI mobilisation.The Punjab government has imposed Section 144 across the province from September 23 to October 5, restricting public gatherings of five or more people on roads and in public places. Authorities have also sought the deployment of Pakistan Rangers in Rawalpindi, Attock, Jhelum and Mianwali.The restrictions have been imposed citing security concerns. A provincial notification referred to a "serious and imminent threat" to public peace and safety from militant and terrorist organisations and hostile intelligence agencies.The planned protest comes amid the detention of three of Imran Khan's sisters. Aleema Khan was detained last week, followed by Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi, who were detained for 30 days under the Punjab maintenance of public order ordinance.On Thursday, the Lahore high court refused to immediately suspend the detention orders against Uzma and Noreen. The court issued notices to the respondents and sought their replies before taking up the plea further.The detentions have added to tensions ahead of the September 27 mobilisation.According to Dawn, lawyers for Uzma and Noreen told the Lahore high court that the two women were "non-political" and had been detained without sufficient legal justification. The court decided to wait for the authorities' response before ruling on their request to suspend the detention orders.Kasim had earlier criticised the detention of his aunts and other relatives and called for international attention to the issue.“This is a disgrace. Now my Aunts Dr. Uzma and Noreen, along with my cousins Shershah and Shahrez, have now been abducted as well. They have broken into my aunties' and cousins' houses and forced them into vehicles with no explanation. No reasons for arrest have been stated," he said in a post on X.Pakistani authorities have said the preventive detentions and restrictions are linked to public-order and security concerns. The Punjab government's notification specifically cited threats from militant organisations and other security risks while announcing the province-wide restrictions.The September 27 PTI protest is expected to add to the political and security pressure surrounding Imran Khan's continued incarceration, with authorities tightening restrictions and increasing security in areas linked to the planned mobilisation.
Article Summary: Kasim Khan urges supporters not to march towards Rawalpindi's Adiala jail during the party's planned September 27 protest. He warns that such a move could be used as a pretext for a "counter" assault on the prison and put his father's life at risk. Security measures have been stepped up across Punjab ahead of the protest.

Article Title: Jamui molestation case: Tejashwi Yadav accuses Bihar CM of violating POCSO by sharing victim’s photo
Article Text:
Opposition leader Tejashwi Yadav (R) accused Bihar CM (L) of breaching the POCSO Act

What happened in Jamui?





PATNA: Bihar chief minister Samrat Choudhary on Thursday drew criticism from the opposition RJD for allegedly revealing the identity of a minor girl who was molested a few days ago in Jamui district.The minor, along with her family, met Choudhary and was assured of “speedy justice” and “strongest possible punishments to all culprits within a month through speedy trial”, officials said.Choudhary shared a photograph of himself with the victim and her family members on his X handle.The post was subsequently taken down, news agency PTI reported.RJD national working president Tejashwi Yadav saved a screenshot of the post and targeted the BJP leader.Sharing the screenshot on X, Yadav, the leader of the opposition in the state assembly, criticised the chief minister, calling him “foolish and inept”.He accused Choudhary of “violating the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act”.Yadav, who is also a former deputy chief minister, alleged that Choudhary had failed in his Class VII exam and was convicted in seven murders, PTI reported.“The BJP leader deserves the strongest possible punishment for violating provisions of the POCSO Act ,” Yadav said.“The way chief minister Samrat Choudhary has violated the POCSO Act. Bihar Police should immediately invoke the POCSO Act against him,” Yadav said.He further questioned, “If the police have invoked the Act against 80-90 people in Jamui and elsewhere, why is the Chief Minister being spared?”The screenshot was also shared by Yadav’s eldest sister, Misa Bharti, the RJD MP from Patliputra. She urged the Bihar Police to “lodge an FIR against the CM,” PTI reported.Bharti alleged that Choudhary revealed the identity of the minor victim even as those who had uploaded videos of the molestation were being booked by the Bihar Police for violating the girl’s privacy.Meanwhile, RJD MP Misa Bharti on Friday alleged that the Bihar government had failed to prevent incidents against women and girls in the state.Speaking at the Sachivalaya police station, she said an FIR naming more than 250 people had been registered in the Jamui case, but questioned why the chief minister had called the minor and her family for a “PR photo session”.Bharti alleged that Choudhary, who is also the state home minister, had violated the POCSO Act by sharing the photograph and said the administration should have focused on preventing such incidents instead.She also questioned the police over the registration of her FIR, saying, “If my FIR is not being registered here, you can imagine the plight of the poor in Bihar.”The minor girl, a Class 10 student, and a Class 10 boy, both friends and residents of Jamui town, were returning from coaching classes on a scooter on September 19 when a group of youths allegedly stopped them in the Sadar police station area.The girl was allegedly surrounded and the boy was separated from her.Videos that later surfaced online purportedly showed several youths questioning the girl, subjecting her to inappropriate physical contact and allegedly dragging her on the road.Police said the episode was believed to have continued for around 20 minutes, though only portions were captured in the videos.The incident was not initially reported to police by the victims or their families.Police took cognisance after the footage surfaced on social media, traced the victims using a vehicle registration number visible in the video and registered an FIR under the POCSO Act and relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).All accused in the case have been arrested.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Bihar chief minister Samrat Choudhary drew criticism from the opposition RJD. He allegedly revealed the identity of a minor girl who was molested a few days ago in Jamui district. The minor, along with her family, was assured of “speedy justice” and “strongest possible punishments to all culprits’.

Article Title: Trump assassination attempt victim James Copenhaver dies at 76
Article Text:
Trump pays tribute as 2024 rally shooting victim James Copenhaver dies

James Copenhaver, who was among those injured in the 2024 shooting at then-Republican presidential nominee Donald Trump's campaign rally, died, his family told CNN.Copenhaver was injured when a gunman opened fire at Trump's campaign rally in Pennsylvania's Butler, on July 13, 2024, during the presidential election campaign.Trump paid tribute to Copenhaver in a post on Truth Social, saying, "God bless American Patriot and Warrior, James Copenhaver, and his incredible family. May he rest in peace!!!"Copenhaver, 76, died on Wednesday at a hospital, according to the Allegheny County Office of the Medical Examiner.His cause of death was not disclosed.Trump was speaking on stage before thousands of supporters at the Butler rally when a gunman positioned on a nearby roof opened fire. Trump was struck in the ear and quickly taken off the stage with blood visible on his face.Copenhaver, who was from Moon Township, and another rally attendee were seriously wounded in the shooting. Corey Comperatore, 50, was killed.The gunman, 20-year-old Thomas Crooks, fired eight rounds during the attack. He was later shot and killed by a US Secret Service counter-sniper team.Trump survived the assassination attempt and continued his campaign for the 2024 presidential election and assumed highest-office again after electoral victory.
Article Summary: James Copenhaver, 76, died on Wednesday at a hospital, according to the Allegheny County Office of the Medical Examiner. He was injured when a gunman opened fire at Trump's campaign rally in Pennsylvania's Butler, on July 13, 2024, during the presidential election campaign.

Article Title: Noida bus fire: Families struggle to identify charred bodies, use anklet, other clues; 6 named
Article Text:
Nine passengers were killed after the bus, travelling from Delhi to Mahoba in Uttar Pradesh, caught fire late Wednesday night





NOIDA: For families of the nine people killed when a sleeper bus caught fire on the Yamuna Expressway, the tragedy deepened at a Sector 94 post-mortem house on Friday, where relatives struggled to identify their loved ones because of the extensive burns.Police have so far identified six of the nine deceased.The bus, travelling from Kashmere Gate in Delhi to Mahoba in Uttar Pradesh, caught fire around 11.20pm on Wednesday near the 33-km milestone of the expressway, killing nine passengers, according to officials.At the Sector 94 post-mortem house, relatives waited anxiously as they tried to identify the bodies.Among them was Sarvagya, son of Rekha Bhardwaj, an injured passenger who survived the incident.Rekha had been travelling with her husband, Devendra Sahay Bhardwaj, who died in the fire.Sarvagya said his father, a retired teacher from a university in Hisar, Haryana, and his mother were travelling to Mahoba to attend the last rites of his grandmother.Siblings Shivam and Nancy also spent hours at the mortuary after learning about the bus fire.They eventually identified the bodies of their mother and brother after considerable difficulty and were seen consoling each other while waiting for officials to complete the formalities.In another case, Ayushi, the granddaughter of one of the deceased, identified the body with the help of an anklet that had been gifted by her son, highlighting the difficulties families faced in identifying victims because of the extensive burns.Police have identified six of the deceased as Shruti Rawat, 31, a resident of Chhatarpur in Madhya Pradesh; Saroj Gupta, 52, and Mayank Gupta, 28, both residents of Mughalpuria Bazar in Rath, Hamirpur; Devendra Sahay Bhardwaj, 60, a resident of Chandra Nagar village in Hisar, Haryana; Har Sharan Gupta, 55, a resident of Balaji Palace in Rajendra Nagar under Orai police station in Jalaun district; and Usha Devi, 65, a resident of Main Road, Muskura, Hamirpur.Police have arrested two drivers and a conductor in connection with the incident. The drivers were identified as Pawan and Yogesh Dixit, both residents of Kanpur Dehat, while the conductor was identified as Rohit, also a resident of Kanpur Dehat.During interrogation, the accused told police that they were travelling from Kashmere Gate to Mahoba on Wednesday night. They allegedly abandoned the vehicle and fled after it suddenly caught fire.An FIR has been registered under BNS Sections 281 (rash driving), 125(b) (endangering life) and 105 (culpable homicide), among others, police said.Rajesh Mohan, a Public Transport Officer with the Gautam Buddh Nagar Regional Transport Office, told PTI that the bus had accumulated fines totalling Rs 1.75 lakh through 19 challans.The bus is operated by Raj Kalpana Travel Agency of Madhya Pradesh but is registered in Madhubani, Bihar, the official said.Additional District Magistrate Ajeet Kumar Singh said on Thursday that the fire was caused by a short circuit and that 35 passengers were onboard, nine of whom died.The injured passengers were provided first aid before being transported to Mahoba in a special vehicle, Singh said.(With PTI inputs)
Article Summary: The bus was travelling from Kashmere Gate in Delhi to Mahoba in Uttar Pradesh. It caught fire around 11.20pm on Wednesday near the 33-km milestone of the expressway. Police have arrested two drivers and a conductor in connection with the incident.

Article Title: America laughs as Trump pivots from 'Kung Flu' to hug Xi’s panda diplomacy
Article Text:
President Donald Trump and China's President Xi Jinping walk along the Colonnade of the White House, Thursday, Sept. 24, 2026, in Washington. (AP Photo/Jacquelyn Martin)

TOI correspondent from Washington: Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived in Washington DC to negotiate trade, technology, tariffs and the future of the global economy. Instead, he got the most elaborate housewarming party ever thrown by a man desperate to impress his guest.A gobsmacked America is cracking up at US President Donald Trump’s over-the-top reception for Xi, with folks wondering “where Kung flu” -- a reference to the MAGA supremo’s needling nickname for Covid, for which he has long blamed China.One commentator compared Trump's welcome of Xi to a nine-year-old showing off his bedroom -- with legos, video games and bunk beds -- to a friend, before transferring the analogy to the White House, where the US President showed off his gilded Oval office, his presidential hall of fame, and a helipad -- which one wag noted the Chinese would have built in two days, if not two hours.Another joked that Trump sounded like “a Long Island mom trying to set her adult daughter up on a date.” A third transformed Trump’s airport welcome of Xi into an imaginary presidential ride-sharing service called “Uber Trump.” The joke: Why summon an ordinary driver when the president himself can pick you up?Not known for fawning over any one, astonished American commentators wondered if Trump had offered Xi a pair of slippers for a sleepover at the White House, thrown rose petals at the foot of his bed, and asked him whether he wanted the guest Wi-Fi password.As it turned out, Xi kept his distance, staying at the Waldorf Astoria, a few blocks from the White House, and not even at Blair House, which is right opposite the White House and typically hosts state guests. Aside: Xi stayed at Blair House during his 2015 visit; and the property that is now Waldorf Astoria was formerly a Trump hotel.The comedy began even before Xi had reached the ceremonial reception, with the image of Trump wincing at the noise from US bombers launching a thousand quips. “Trump picked him up at the airport? That is friendship. I don’t even pick my own kid up at the airport!” gagged Desi Lydic on the Daily Show, joking that Trump recoiling at the roar of a US bomber flying overhead was like a child startled by the noise of its own fart. "For a man who's always screaming about China, Hairman Mao laid it on very thick today,” joked Jimmy Kimmel.There was also food. Fallon contrasted the elegant Chinese-influenced dishes at the dinner banquet with Trump’s preferred “two Big Mac with large fries and a diet coke,” while Kimmel warned that China sending pandas to the US was a bad idea because Trump may just eat them. "I'm not saying Trump is sucking up to him, but the Kennedy Center is now called the Xi Kennedy Center," Fallon quipped.Across both late-night stages and social media, the jokes clustered around the same themes: the extravagant, almost childlike eagerness of the reception (airport pickup, red carpets, renovation tours, helipad pride); the contrast with Trump’s earlier hard-line China bluster; the superficiality of the pageantry versus unresolved issues; food contrasts (elegant Chinese-American fusion versus Trump’s fast-food preferences); and the panda gift as both charming and comically mismatched.The humor treated the summit less as high diplomacy and more as a high-production personal friendship performance, with Trump’s fawning providing the punchlines, including an observation from Seth Meyers that "not even Chinese citizens gush this much about Xi." The short trade-truce extension and absence of any major breakthroughs only sharpened the focus on the optics, offering plenty of fire for satire.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump threw an over-the-top reception for Chinese President Xi Jinping. One commentator compared Trump's welcome of Xi to a nine-year-old showing off his bedroom to a friend. Another joked that Trump sounded like “a Long Island mom trying to set her adult daughter up on a date”

Article Title: IIT Bombay student suicide: Sahil Wakode’s parents spend 8 hours at Crime Branch office amid probe
Article Text:
Sahil's parents, Ravindra and Sonali Wakode, began a hunger strike at Azad Maidan in Mumbai





MUMBAI: The parents of IIT Bombay student Sahil Wakode, who died by suicide on September 18, spent around eight hours at the Bandra West office of the Mumbai Crime Branch on Friday, an official said.They arrived at 10am and left around 6pm.While their statements had been recorded during an earlier visit, Crime Branch officials did not say whether any additional information or statements were recorded during Friday's session, news agency PTI reported.The Crime Branch has so far recorded statements of 20 people in connection with the case, while efforts are underway to access Wakode's locked mobile phone.Wakode's parents have alleged that their son faced caste discrimination at the institute. They staged a hunger strike at Azad Maidan on Thursday, seeking action against his "tormentors".Union minister of state for social justice and empowerment Ramdas Athawale meanwhile visited IIT Bombay and sought a thorough investigation into Wakode's death, PTI reported.As per the preliminary investigation, Sahil Wakode, 22, a student in the Department of Energy Science and Engineering, went directly to his hostel room after leaving the examination hall on September 18.The institute had initially said that he was caught using an AI-platform on his mobile phone during the examination. When he did not emerge from his room by around 7pm, the door was opened and he was found dead inside.Among the 20 people questioned so far are students who were present in the examination hall, invigilators and various administrative officials, police said.Wakode's mobile phone was secured with a pattern lock, restricting access, though several missed call notifications were visible on the display screen, a police official said.Forensic experts were trying to access the device, PTI reported.IIT Bombay faculty member Suryanarayan Doolla, who has been named in the police FIR alleging abetment to suicide on grounds of caste discrimination, has been sent on leave to facilitate an impartial probe into the case.Wakode's parents, Ravindra and Sonali Wakode, began a hunger strike at Azad Maidan in Mumbai on Thursday, alleging that their son repeatedly faced caste discrimination at the institute.They left the ground at night.During his visit to IIT Bombay, Athawale, a prominent Dalit leader from Maharashtra, discussed the matter with the institute's director and senior officials. He also visited Wakode's hostel room, officials said."Any student who gets admission to the IIT is very clever and highly capable. Sahil’s death should be thoroughly investigated and action should be taken against those responsible,” the minister said.“The way he died by suicide suggests there could be some major reason behind it. Someone may have insulted him and forced him to take the extreme step,” Athawale said.Athawale said he would discuss the issue with Union education minister Pralhad Joshi, PTI reported.The institute has apologised twice over its earlier communication indicating that Sahil died by suicide hours after allegedly being caught using ChatGPT during an exam.Some TV channels aired CCTV footage from the examination hall showing Sahil's movements before a professor approached him and led him away from the hall.Police said the CCTV footage was being used to reconstruct the sequence of events.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: The parents of IIT Bombay student Sahil Wakode spent around eight hours at the Bandra West office of the Mumbai Crime Branch on Friday. Wakode's parents have alleged that their son faced caste discrimination at the institute. They staged a hunger strike at Azad Maidan on Thursday, seeking action against his "tormentors"

Article Title: Trump's 48 F-35 jets for Saudi Arabia: Why is Israel uneasy and China a key concern
Article Text:
US President Donald Trump with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman during a “coffee ceremony” at the Saudi Royal Court on May 13, 2025, in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

The F-35I – also known as the Adir – a custom variant based on the Alpha, redesigned, and modified by the Israeli Defence Force.

Numbers not the real worry

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, however, reportedly played down its significance of Trump's deal with Saudi Arabia.

Presence of US bases across Middle East.

China's shadow over the deal

US President Donald Trump and Saudi Crown Prince and Prime Minister Mohammed bin Salman laugh during a meeting in the Oval Office at the White House in Washington, November 18, 2025.

The burden of broken promises

Yes, Saudi Arabia restarted operations at its East-West oil pipeline on September 22, 2026, after a temporary shutdown caused by drone strikes.

The rival camp Riyadh has been building

Why Israel worries

The Trump administration has agreed to put the world's most advanced combat aircraft in Saudi hands. It comes at a time when Gulf allies are questioning whether American primacy still carries weight. And nowhere is that question more important than in the ever-conflicted region of West Asia.Washington's approach to West Asia has long resembled digging a hole to bury sand, only to be left with a new heap of sand, creating a loop that keeps the digging going.Trump's decision to approve the $24.3 billion sale of F-35s to the Saudis, when the Kingdom is being bogged down by the Iran-backed Houthis, appears to be the latest turn of the spade.Though it is meant to steady a Gulf partner shaken by Iranian fire and doubts about American guarantees, the aircraft deal has opened a fresh cavity for Israel, until now the only country in the region to fly the world's most powerful combat aircraft.Under the deal, the state department has notified Congress of a possible sale of 48 jets, with engines and support, which would make Saudi Arabia the second country in the Middle East to fly the aircraft after Israel.However, the Saudi jets will reportedly not have all the advanced features of the F-35s operated by Israel.The F-35I, also known as the Adir, a custom variant based on the Alpha, redesigned, and modified by the Israeli Defence Force (IDF). Although strictly forbidden, after negotiations the US defence force reluctantly gave permission for Israeli designers to make certain modifications to the F-35A design.Production and delivery would take years, but the political signal is immediate, with some Israeli officials raising concerns that the deal could erode their country's "qualitative military edge" -- a standard that American policymakers have sought to protect since the 1973 war and that Congress has mandated.Israel bought 50 F-35s in two rounds, in 2016 and 2017, although several reports suggest two have yet to arrive. That leaves 48 on the ground, the same number Riyadh has requested.However, Israel will not stay level for long, since its defence ministry plans 25 more jets from 2028 and has announced a further squadron of unspecified size.The anxiety is therefore about something less measurable. When Donald Trump first confirmed he was considering the sale last November, Israeli officials told Axios they did not oppose it as such, but wanted it "to be subject to Saudi normalisation with Israel". That condition has not been met, and no such deal appears close.A security source told CNN at the time that Saudi Arabia acquiring "the same capabilities" was "very concerning". Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, however, reportedly played down its significance.Meanwhile, Washington has maintained that regional balance will hold as "the proposed sale of this equipment and support will not alter the military balance in the region". Interestingly, whether Israel accepts that assurance will depend less on the wording than on who Riyadh chooses to stand with in the years ahead.The strongest objection in Washington concerns Beijing, with a defense intelligence agency assessment, issued months ago, questioning whether American and Saudi personnel could secure the sites that would hold F-35 technology.It also flagged the access Chinese military personnel have to Saudi bases and the kingdom's heavy use of Chinese telecommunications technology in its infrastructure and defence installations.An earlier assessment had already questioned the growing partnership, in which China sells Saudi Arabia ballistic missiles and helps it learn to build them.Representative Raja Krishnamoorthi, a Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee, put the fear plainly. "It could put the crown jewels of American military technology within reach of the Chinese Communist Party," he said.There is also a precedent when Trump announced an F-35 sale to the United Arab Emirates (UAE) in 2020, and the Biden administration ended the process over similar worries about Abu Dhabi's links with China.For Israel, the risk is indirect; it's highly unlikely that Riyadh, which is absorbing Iranian missile and drone attacks, would hand secrets to Tehran.The concern is leakage through third parties. The US intelligence agencies worry that Chinese spies could target Saudi networks, maintenance sites and personnel, a task made easier by Chinese military personnel's access to Saudi bases and by Chinese technology in the Kingdom's telecommunications and defence installations.Understanding why Riyadh might gradually hedge against America in the future, potentially against Israel's interests, helps trace how American security promises have fared over the years.The 2003 invasion of Iraq, launched with great confidence in what military force could achieve, ended in a costly occupation and shook the regional order, though that order eventually reassembled.In 2011, the fall of Egypt's Hosni Mubarak convinced Arab autocrats they could not count on Washington to save them from domestic upheaval. Several set out to contain threats themselves, often with devastating results.Doubts about deterrence against Iran grew denser after Washington did not respond to a 2019 attack on Saudi oil refineries attributed to Iran, and Houthi drone strikes on the UAE in 2022 deepened the unease.The 2026 war with Iran did the most damage as Gulf leaders were seemingly angry that the United States and Israel launched it without consulting them, in the middle of Omani-brokered talks with Tehran.Iran struck every Gulf state but concentrated on Bahrain and the UAE, both Abraham Accords signatories. Missile defences stopped the worst, yet enough got through to cause real harm, and much of the network of American bases was damaged, destroyed or rendered irrelevant.Washington then failed to dislodge the Iranian regime and could not keep the Strait of Hormuz open. American strikes on Iranian water storage facilities, and Israeli strikes on oil depots, alarmed Gulf capitals that feared reprisals against their own water and nuclear sites.Even Riyadh's long-sought nuclear agreement was left in limbo when Trump changed its terms a day after it was finalised.Moreover, Mohammed bin Salman, the Kingdom's Crown Prince, is reportedly unhappy with Trump's refusal to provide direct military support to Saudi Arabia in its fight against the Houthis. Particarly after the its key East-West oil pipeline was hit in the attack.That makes the F-35 deal look less like a favour and more like a transaction, which Trump has ensured with all his key allies, even Europe.Summing up that sentiment, retired US Lieutenant General Karen Gibson put it aptly: "MBS will not forget."Before the fighting began at the end of February, Saudi Arabia had started assembling a bloc of its own. Riyadh drew Egypt, Pakistan, Qatar and Turkey into a coalition meant to counter the American-backed Emirati-Israeli alliance.This matters a great deal for the F-35 question. The country due to receive the aircraft that anchors Israel's air power has been organising against an alignment that includes Israel.Also, Riyadh's rivalry with Abu Dhabi runs deep. Saudi Arabia backs the post-Assad government in Syria, while the UAE shares Israel's hostility towards it. In Yemen, Riyadh recently drove out Emirati proxies, and it has complained that the UAE promotes secessionist movements that undermine regional stability.Also, the UAE coordinated with Israel and the United States on strikes against Iranian targets. Riyadh watches that alignment uneasily, seeing it as a threat to its own leadership.Turkey adds another layer as Netanyahu has already called President Recep Tayyip Erdogan "not exactly a model ally of the United States", a remark he made after Trump said in July that he was weighing F-35 sales to Ankara as well. Israel thus faces advanced American jets flowing to more than one capital whose interests diverge from its own.Arab allies who have lost faith in Washington, sooner or later, will increasingly exercise their autonomy, which could mean diplomacy with Iran and closer ties with China and Russia, whatever American officials prefer.Saudi Arabia has precedent here, having reached a rapprochement with Iran in 2023. Some Gulf states may now seek side deals with Tehran to stay off its target list. For a kingdom under Iranian fire, that is prudence rather than defection.Yet a fifth-generation fleet needs decades of spares, software and training, so it presumes a buyer whose alignment stays put. None of this points to an imminent break, and Gulf states may even deepen ties with Washington in the short term. A Saudi Arabia that talks to Tehran, buys Chinese missiles and uses Chinese telecommunications networks is a partner whose direction Israel cannot easily read.Congress has been given 30 days to review the sale and could pass a joint resolution of disapproval, but it would need two-thirds of both chambers to survive a veto. The House is in recess until November and the Senate is about to follow, so blocking the sale looks improbable. Any safeguards will have to be secured well before delivery.Saudi Arabia, under fire, remains by far the biggest buyer of American weapons, and interoperability with US and allied forces has genuine value.But the deeper question is whether an advanced weapon, under a purely transactional agreement, can secure loyalty against the backdrop of wobbling US guarantees? That, more than any tally of jets, is what perhaps unsettles Israel.
Article Summary: Trump administration has agreed to put the world's most advanced combat aircraft in Saudi hands. It comes at a time when Gulf allies are questioning whether American primacy still carries weight. Saudi Arabia restarted operations at its East-West oil pipeline on September 22, 2026.

Article Title: Strong waves & swell surge: Red alert issued in all coastal districts of Keralam
Article Text:
Until Incois withdraws the warning, all activities, including beach-centered tourism should be completely avoided

Kochi:





Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (Incois) has declared a red alert in all coastal districts of Keralam. The agency has warned that coastal areas of the state could experience strong waves and swell surge phenomenon.Incois has warned that there is a possibility of high waves ranging from 1.0 to 1.5 metres and sea swell along Kerala coast from 2.30am on Saturday to 2.30am on Monday. In coastal zones, especially in low-lying areas, there is a possibility of inundation and swell surge.A vigilance warning for high waves and the swell surge has been issued for Kanyakumari, Ramanathapuram, Thoothukudi, Tirunelveli coasts of Tamil Nadu and Lakshadweep coasts as well. Since there is a possibility of swell surge, fishermen and coastal residents should exercise extreme caution.Until Incois withdraws the warning, all activities, including beach-centred tourism, should be completely avoided. Fishing vessels should be safely tied and secured at the harbour. Maintaining a safe distance between vessels can avoid the risk of accidents due to collision. The safety of fishing equipment should be ensured.Trips to the beach and recreational activities in the sea should be completely avoided.
Article Summary: Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (Incois) has declared a red alert in all coastal districts of Keralam. The agency has warned that coastal areas of the state could experience strong waves and swell surge phenomenon. Until Incois withdraws the warning, all activities, including beach- centered tourism should be completely avoided.

Article Title: Trump embraces Xi as peer, alarms partners and critics
Article Text: TOI correspondent from Washington: A 48-hour state visit to the United States by China’s President Xi Jinping yielded no immediate major breakthroughs but confirmed the broad impression, in visuals and much as words, that Washington now accepts China as a peer in a new G-2 formulation.For all the talk of trade, artificial intelligence, Taiwan, Iran and strategic competition, the most consequential message of Xi’s visit may have been the choreography itself. A fawning Trump repeatedly described Xi as a friend and the relationship as a “great friendship,” with little personal reciprocity from the Chinese leader.The charitable explanation for what many critics said was Trump’s folding before Xi and muting his demands from and tirades against China was purportedly in the service of American farmers – his major voting bloc – who are getting screwed because Beijing cut down purchase of soy, corn, and other farm produce. In brief remarks during a tea ceremony, the MAGA supremo mentioned that the visit had yielded “great results” for American farmers without elaborating, but spoke of little else other than accepting Xi’s invitation to visit China.By most accounts, the summit produced a lot of optics, but little else, amid a cascade of criticism that Trump is placating China rather than confronting it over its actions inimical to US, including its tacit support for Iran.The most withering censure came from Republican Senator John Kennedy of Louisiana, who likened Xi and leaders of Russia, North Korea and Iran, to reptiles. "The chief reptile, the quarterback, is President Xi. They all lie like timeshare salesmen. You can’t trust them. I wouldn’t turn my back on any of them, even if I thought and knew they were two days dead,” Kennedy told a TV show during the visit. Even Senator Chuck Grassley, the Iowa Republican whose state is deeply dependent on agricultural exports, was sceptical about the outcome of the visit, saying that if extending the trade truce was all that emerged, the summit risked becoming a “show job" for a communist autocrat.On Taiwan, the most sensitive strategic issue between the two sides, there was no public breakthrough. Trump has continued to hold in abeyance a roughly $14 billion Taiwan weapons package that he described earlier this year as a negotiating chip with Beijing. China wants the arms sales halted; US lawmakers across party lines have urged their release.Nor were there any signs of a significant Chinese concession on Iran. Beijing has expressed interest in peace and stability but remains economically intertwined with Tehran. On advanced chips, Washington also appeared to hold its line, despite Beijing’s interest in easing US technology restrictions. That may ultimately prove more consequential than the ceremonial theatrics. The summit thus produced no obvious quid pro quo in which China would use its leverage over Iran in return for a major American concession.Trump’s defenders argued though that the president’s approach should be judged against what they described as decades of failed China policy under previous administrations. “Obama and Biden talked tough, but gave away American factories to the Chinese. Trump actually launched a trade war against China,” noted Brian Kilmeade on Fox News, pointing out that Trump "kicked the Chinese out of Panama Canal" and went after their “favourite oil proxies in our hemisphere, Venezuela and Iran, and is about to kick them out of Cuba. ”That in essence is the larger contradiction of the summit. Trump has not abandoned confrontation with China; he has instead recast it as transactional management between two superpowers, much to the consternation of other nations like India, Japan, and South Korea. Xi, for his part, repeatedly spoke not of friendship between two men but of China and the US as “two major countries” with a responsibility to find a new way of coexisting.The symbolism was perhaps captured most neatly by the contrasting tours offered during the two leaders’ encounters. When Trump visited Beijing in May, Xi showed him ancient trees at Zhongnanhai, including specimens more than 1,000 years old — a quiet display of Chinese historical depth and long-term continuity. In Washington, Trump showed Xi his new White House helipad, built in a “record” 12 weeks – which the Chinese would have built in 12 days if not 12 hours.
Article Summary: Xi Jinping's 48-hour state visit to the United States yielded no immediate major breakthroughs but confirmed the broad impression, in visuals and much as words, that Washington now accepts China as a peer in a new G-2 formulation. A fawning Trump repeatedly described Xi as a friend and the relationship as a “great friendship,” with little personal reciprocity from the Chinese leader.

Article Title: ‘No Muslim can even dare’: Pakistan PM at UN condemns Houthi attacks, draws red line over Mecca
Article Text:
Pakistan's PM Shehbaz Sharif speaks at UNGA

NEW DELHI: Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Friday used the 81st United Nations General Assembly to condemn Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and warn against any threat to the safety and sanctity of Mecca.He also defended Pakistan’s new defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Türkiye, while highlighting Islamabad’s diplomatic efforts to bring the United States and Iran to the negotiating table."We once again condemn, in the strongest possible terms, the recent deplorable attacks by the Houthis against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia," Sharif said in his address."The attempted drone attack on the holy city of Mecca al-Mukarramah has outraged Muslims across the globe. Any threat to safety and sanctity... is a red line that must never be crossed. No Muslim can even dare to think of committing such a heinous (act)."Saudi Arabia has accused the Houthis of targeting Mecca with a drone, an allegation the Houthis denied. Riyadh has also reported intercepting Houthi ballistic missiles following renewed hostilities in the region.Sharif also sought to underline Islamabad’s diplomatic role in the conflict between the United States and Iran, saying Pakistan had worked to bring the two sides to the negotiating table.“Pakistan chose to act swiftly through concerted efforts. Pakistan successfully brought Washington and Tehran under one roof in Islamabad. From the Islamabad talks to the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, many historic steps were taken to bring an end to this serious conflict,” he said.The Pakistani prime minister also referred to the recently signed defence agreement between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye. The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement provides for collective defence commitments among the three countries, while Pakistani officials have said the arrangement is not directed against any particular state.Sharif said the pact was intended to serve defence, stability and peace rather than confrontation.On Palestine, Sharif denounced what he called Israel’s “genocidal agenda” and condemned what he described as “Israeli aggression against Lebanon and Syria”.He also thanked Pakistan’s Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff, Field Marshal Asim Munir, crediting his “relentless efforts” with helping create “space for diplomacy under exceptionally difficult and challenging circumstances”.Sharif further thanked US President Donald Trump for what he called his “timely intervention” during the 2025 India-Pakistan conflict, saying it had “saved hundreds of millions of lives in South Asia”.His remarks came as Pakistan balances its ties with Iran with its deepening strategic and defence relationship with Saudi Arabia, while regional tensions continue to test Islamabad’s stated preference for diplomacy.
Article Summary: Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif used the 81st United Nations General Assembly to condemn Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. He also defended Pakistan’s new defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Türkiye, while highlighting Islamabad's diplomatic efforts to bring the United States and Iran to the negotiating table.

Article Title: All-women SIT to probe child rape case against Veeramani
Article Text:
Chennai police have established a Special Investigation Team to probe allegations of sexual offences against R Veeramani.





CHENNAI: Tamil Nadu govt has formed a four-member all-women IPS officers’ special investigation team (SIT) to probe the child rape case against the granite baron, R Veeramani, and other ‘related matters. ’The SIT will be headed by additional commissioner of police PC Thenmozhi of the Central Crime Branch in Chennai city police. The other members are: Joint commissioner of police N Disha Mittal of the West Zone, superintendent of police J Mutharasi, who handles spokesperson and media relations for the DGP's office, and deputy commissioner of police VV Geethanjali of the Central Women and Children (CWC) unit in Chennai city police.The arrest of Veeramani, and his two associates -- Shanthi and Mahendra Simhan -- on August 29 based on a video clipping showing the rape of a child rocked Tamil Nadu, as he was a leading industrialist who had headed several entities including India-Japan Chamber of Commerce and Industry for several years.Police officers, on condition of anonymity, said at least nine more children had recorded their statements saying they too had been similarly raped.A long-time employee of Veeramani’s Gem Granites, Ganesan, too has been arrested for being in possession of video clippings of child rapes.Assistant commissioner of police Yasmin was shunted out of her present post as assistant commissioner of Koyambedu, as she was the one who filed a “further action dropped” report before a special court for Pocso cases and tried to close the case.The SIT has been tasked with probing the rape case as well as other “related matters” amidst political and social outcry over the suspected attempts to close the case under “further action dropped” category. Police have been examining evidence and statements collected during the investigation, including digital material linked to the case.The SIT will coordinate the investigation and examine the evidence and statements collected so far as part of the continuing probe.
Article Summary: Chennai police have established a Special Investigation Team to probe allegations of sexual offences against R Veeramani. The SIT has been tasked with probing the rape case as well as other ‘related matters’ amidst political and social outcry over the suspected attempts to close the case.

Article Title: Mark Zuckerberg’s $300 million superyacht docked in Japan for the first time, Launchpad has a new neighbour, the billionaire who once wanted Meta suspend its Japanese operations
Article Text:
The legal feud: A 1-Yen lawsuit against Meta

Launchpad cruised from Alaska to Asia

Mark Zuckerberg’s $300 million superyacht, Launchpad, seems to be on a ‘world tour’. The vessel recently docked in Japan for the first time, pulling into port right beside a newly delivered megayacht owned by Japanese e-commerce billionaire Yusaku Maezawa. What makes this extraordinary scene along the Minato Mirai waterfront is the fact that Maezawa is an outspoken critic, and is currently suing Meta in court. Maezawa’s 114.2-meter vessel, Nausicaä, was stationed at Shinko Pier No. 8 since September 5. Zuckerberg’s 118-meter Launchpad arrived shortly after following a trans-Pacific crossing from Alaska. While there is no confirmation that either billionaire is aboard, the shared berth creates a dramatic visual standoff between two corporate adversaries whose high-profile dispute continues through the Japanese legal system.The proximity of the two ships is striking given Maezawa’s two-year legal battle against Zuckerberg's social networking empire. In May 2024, Maezawa filed a lawsuit against Meta Platforms and its regional Facebook Japan unit, over a string of fake investment schemes that used his name and likeness without permission.Rather than seeking financial restitution, Maezawa demanded a symbolic payout of just ¥1 (less than a single US cent) alongside an injunction, using the case to legally test whether tech platforms can be held liable for hosting criminal advertisements.When Meta fought the claims and sought a dismissal during initial hearings in July 2024, Maezawa intensified his criticisms. By August 2025, with unauthorised ads still surfacing, Maezawa accused foreign tech firms of enabling online fraud for advertising profits, arguing that Meta was “completely looking down on Japan” and demanding penalties up to the outright suspension of its Japanese operations.Launchpad reached Yokohama after an active summer cruising southeastern Alaska, making stops across Juneau, Petersburg and Ketchikan. Marine tracking logs confirmed the vessel cleared Juneau on September 1 to start its voyage across the Pacific. Automated tracking lists Singapore as its subsequent destination, indicating that the stop in Japan is part of an ongoing Asian itinerary.During its passage through Alaskan waters, the yacht was linked to a minor overnight incident around 1:00 am involving a small recreational craft requiring support. Observers aboard the small cruise ship Wilderness Legacy noted that Launchpad slowed nearby but did not intervene before the cruise ship assisted the boater.While Zuckerberg and Maezawa have no reported plans to meet while their ships share the harbor, their vessels have set up an ironic encounter in Yokohama—anchoring one of tech's most unusual international rivalries directly along the Japanese coast.
Article Summary: Mark Zuckerberg's $300 million superyacht, Launchpad, has docked in Japan for the first time. The vessel pulled into port right beside a newly delivered megayacht owned by Japanese e-commerce billionaire Yusaku Maezawa. There is no confirmation that either billionaire is aboard, but the shared berth creates a dramatic visual standoff.

Article Title: ‘Met us like guardian’: Jamui molestation victim’s mother praises Bihar CM, govt response
Article Text:
The mother of the minor girl allegedly molested in Bihar’s Jamui said chief minister Samrat Choudhary met her family “like a guardian”.





JAMUI: The mother of the minor girl allegedly molested in Bihar’s Jamui said chief minister Samrat Choudhary met her family “like a guardian” and assured them of her daughter’s safety and education.“When he met us, it did not feel like he was the chief minister of Bihar; he met us like a guardian,” the woman said. She said Choudhary blessed her daughter and told her, “You are a very brave girl,” while assuring the family that they could approach him without hesitation if they needed anything.The victim’s mother also praised the administration for the swift action in the case, saying the family had received “a lot of support and cooperation”.She referred to the police action, including the shooting of the main accused in the leg during an encounter.The mother’s comments came after she and her family met Choudhary following the September 19 incident in which the Class 10 girl and a male classmate were allegedly stopped by a group of youths while returning from coaching classes.The girl was allegedly surrounded and molested, while the boy was separated from her.Videos of the incident later surfaced on social media, prompting police to register a case under the POCSO Act and relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Police had initially identified around seven people allegedly involved in the incident and arrested three. The main accused was later shot in the leg during a police encounter, according to police sources.The victim’s mother said the family was satisfied with the government’s response and that the chief minister had assured them about her daughter’s education and safety.She also appealed to people across Bihar and the country to support victims of such crimes.“We would like society, the people of Jamui, the people of Bihar and the people of the country to support every daughter in the same way they have supported my daughter, so that no daughter or her family ever hesitates to seek punishment for a criminal,” she said.Meanwhile, the mother of the main accused has alleged that police staged the encounter and claimed her son was shot after being forced to run.Police had earlier said the accused was shot in the leg during an encounter in the Town Police Station area.
Article Summary: The mother of the minor girl allegedly molested in Bihar’s Jamui said chief minister Samrat Choudhary met her family “like a guardian” She said he blessed her daughter and told her, “You are a very brave girl,” while assuring the family that they could approach him without hesitation if they needed anything. The victim's mother praised the administration for the swift action in the case.
